repositories.name: platform-contracts
repositories.reason: Source of truth for every changed contract: add optional column tags/classification fields to ingestion.schema.discovered.v1 and metadata.dataset.changed.v1, column classification + new steward PUT endpoint in metadata-graph OpenAPI, masked_columns in the entitlements Decision and query response, and a classification selector in dq-api rule bindings, released as minor 2.4.0.

repositories.name: platform-sdk
repositories.reason: Typed SDK models drop undeclared fields (ADR-004), so MetadataClient column models need classification/tags plus a set-classification method, EntitlementsClient Decision needs masked_columns, and the SDK must pin contracts 2.4.0 so publish validation accepts the new event fields.

repositories.name: metadata-graph
repositories.reason: Owning repo: store classification per column (suggested from source tags, steward-overridable and sticky across re-ingestion), expose it in GET columns and a new PUT classification endpoint, and include it in metadata.dataset.changed.v1 payloads.

repositories.name: ingestion-service
repositories.reason: Postgres connectors already read column comments with tags such as 'tags: pii,email' but do not propagate them; they must parse and publish them as an optional columns[].tags field on ingestion.schema.discovered.v1.

repositories.name: entitlements-service
repositories.reason: It is the only place access decisions are computed (ADR-007), so it must load column classifications and return masked_columns (PII columns when the principal lacks a pii:read grant) in POST /v1/access/decide.

repositories.name: query-gateway
repositories.reason: It is the single enforcement point that returns data to consumers (ADR-007), so it must mask the columns listed in the decision's masked_columns before returning POST /v1/query results.

repositories.name: dq-engine
repositories.reason: Rules are bound per column by data type today; it must read column classification/tags via MetadataClient.get_columns and bind PII-format validation rules to columns classified PII.

repositories.name: search-indexer
repositories.reason: It validates metadata.dataset.changed.v1 strictly against a vendored schema (contracts 2.1.0, additionalProperties: false) and dead-letters unknown fields, so it must vendor contracts 2.4.0 and be deployed before metadata-graph emits classification.

repositories.name: platform-e2e
repositories.reason: New cross-service behaviour (tag ingest -> classification -> masked query results and PII DQ rules) needs a new end-to-end suite run in the int environment per the change playbook.

repositories.name: lineage-service
repositories.reason: Consumes metadata.dataset.changed.v1 as a tolerant reader of dataset.urn/name only, so it needs only contract-test re-verification against the 2.4.0 payload.

repositories.name: notification-service
repositories.reason: Reads only owner from GET /v1/datasets/{urn} via the SDK and dataset_urn/score from dq.result.published.v1 (tolerant), so new PII rule results need re-verification only.

considered_not_impacted.name: usage-metering
considered_not_impacted.reason: Consumes only gateway.access.logged.v1, which this plan does not change (adding masked_columns for audit is an open question).

considered_not_impacted.name: reporting-service
considered_not_impacted.reason: Decommissioned and archived; the metadata-graph README still lists it as a consumer of metadata.dataset.changed.v1, which is stale.

considered_not_impacted.name: platform-catalog
considered_not_impacted.reason: No new components, APIs, topics or dependency edges are introduced (all changes are within existing APIs/topics), so catalog entities and the generated graph stay valid.

considered_not_impacted.name: architecture-docs
considered_not_impacted.reason: No code; flow docs (access-decision, ingest-to-graph, data-quality) should be updated to describe column-level classification and masking, tracked as a documentation task in the plan.

contracts.name: ingestion.schema.discovered.v1
contracts.description: Add optional columns[].tags (array of lower-case strings parsed from the source column comment, e.g. ["pii","email"]); stays on .v1 per ADR-009, platform-contracts 2.4.0.

contracts.name: metadata.dataset.changed.v1
contracts.description: Add optional dataset.columns[].classification (enum PUBLIC|INTERNAL|CONFIDENTIAL|PII), classification_source (SOURCE_TAG|STEWARD) and tags; classification changes are published with the existing change_type UPDATED (no new enum value). Additive on .v1, but search-indexer (strict) must upgrade first.

contracts.name: GET /v1/datasets/{urn}/columns
contracts.description: Column schema gains optional classification, classification_source, tags and suggested_classification; metadata-graph-api 1.5.0.

contracts.name: PUT /v1/datasets/{urn}/columns/{column}/classification
contracts.description: New steward endpoint: body {classification, reason?}; sets classification_source=STEWARD, returns the updated column, publishes metadata.dataset.changed.v1 (UPDATED); 404 for unknown dataset/column, 400 for invalid value.

contracts.name: POST /v1/access/decide
contracts.description: Decision gains optional masked_columns (array of column names; empty when nothing to mask or principal holds pii:read); allow/reason/policy_id unchanged; entitlements-api 1.3.0.

contracts.name: POST /v1/query
contracts.description: Response gains optional masked_columns (array of column names); row keys unchanged, values of masked columns replaced with the masking token (null by default) when masking is enabled for the environment.

contracts.name: POST /v1/rules
contracts.description: Rule binding gains an optional selector by column classification (and optional tag, e.g. email) alongside the existing data-type selector, so PII-format rules can be bound to PII columns; GET /v1/rules returns the new selector.

open_questions: Should a tag-derived classification be applied immediately as the effective classification (assumed: yes, fail-safe for PII) or held as a suggestion until a steward confirms it?

Exact tag-to-classification mapping: assumed pii->PII, confidential->CONFIDENTIAL, internal->INTERNAL, public->PUBLIC, highest sensitivity wins, other tags (email, phone) kept as PII subtype hints; do untagged columns stay unclassified (null) or default to INTERNAL?
Who may call the steward PUT classification endpoint and how is it authorised (metadata-graph has no auth model in the repo; assumed a steward role/grant checked via entitlements-service)?
Does a pii:read grant type already exist in entitlements-service, and is it global or scoped per dataset/domain?
Masking format: null vs a type-preserving or partial mask (e.g. a***@x.com); null can break consumers that assume non-null for non-nullable columns.

How should query-gateway handle SQL that references PII columns in expressions, aliases, joins, WHERE/GROUP BY or SELECT * (name-based result masking alone is bypassable)? Assumed: resolve output-column lineage and reject (403) queries it cannot mask safely.
Failure behaviour once enforcement is on: if entitlements-service cannot load column classifications, should it deny the request or mask every column (fail closed)?
Should masking be audited by adding optional masked_columns to gateway.access.logged.v1 (would make usage-metering verify_only)?

search-indexer vendors contracts 2.1.0 while current is 2.3.0: did 2.2.0/2.3.0 already add fields to metadata.dataset.changed.v1 that it is dead-lettering? Its DLQ should be checked before the upgrade.
Should search-indexer index classification so catalog search can filter or flag PII columns, or only accept the field?
Which PII-format rules are required (email, phone, national ID, ...) and which tags select them; should PII DQ results be excluded from owner emails or reports that might contain sample values?
Do other channels return column metadata outside metadata-graph (e.g. search results from search-indexer) that also need classification or masking?
Should existing datasets be backfilled (re-run schema discovery for Postgres sources) so classification exists before masking enforcement is switched on?
metadata-graph's README lists reporting-service (decommissioned) as a consumer and omits lineage-service and search-indexer; fix the README in the same PR?
